correctness.rationale: For the explicitly defined forward radius-normalized angular momentum, weak coupling first gives the bounded observable of independent Gaussian noises added to a circle of radius a=R exp(−s), with variances v_i=T_i(1−exp(−2s)). Continuity of the nondegenerate age-conditioned Gaussian law and bounded convergence justify the susceptibility. The circular complex angular average has a residue only for |z|>a; at |z|=a the pole is removable. The anisotropic Gaussian polar integral then has the stated I₁ factor, strictly positive except when the temperatures coincide, with the stated sign. A direct endpoint check sets x=(ρ²−a²)/(2v₊). After factoring exp(−a²/(2v₊)), scaling the remaining amplitude using I₁(z)exp(−z)~(2πz)^(−1/2) gives an integrand dominated by a constant times x exp(−x), with limiting integral 1. The amplitude is 2√(2/π) v₊²/[a³√(v₊−v₋)]. With c=R²/(4T₊), the exponent is −c/s+c+O(s), so the positive magnitude of A(s) is asymptotic to 8T₊² exp(c)s^(3/2) exp(−c/s)/(R³√(π(T₊−T₋))). The K_{5/2} integral gives √π c r^(−1/2) exp(−2√(cr)) after multiplication by r; the large-age error is exponentially negligible and the relative small-age error is bounded by the corresponding positive integral. These factors give the frozen prefactor. The second-moment integral gives the momentum susceptibility separately. This verifies the observable defined in RESULT.md, not a different definition based on the generator acting on a polar-angle branch or on reset chords. The supplied notes and checks/verify.py were inspected but not executed.
